birth.stop: Toulouse, the register at La Grave
birth.date_confidence: Attested by the French civil register of Toulouse and carried by both the English and Spanish Wikipedia articles as the consensus birth record. Coordinates are those of the Hopital de La Grave per Wikipedia (French), 'Hopital de La Grave' (43 36 03 N, 1 26 03 E). The register itself was not fetched in this pass; it reaches this file through the two encyclopaedia articles and through the genealogists Ruffie and Galopa as they cite it.
birth.method: first stop whose year matches the journey's first year

stops.stop: Valle Eden, the birth Uruguay claims
stops.date_confidence: Contested and rejected by the scholarly consensus. The date, place and parentage come from Gardel's own 1920 declaration at the Uruguayan consulate in Buenos Aires and from Uruguayan tradition (Wikipedia (Spanish), 'Carlos Gardel', hipotesis uruguayista); no contemporary document from 1887 corroborates any part of it, and the Toulouse civil register of December 1890 contradicts it. Coordinates are those of Valle Eden per Wikipedia (Spanish), 'Valle Eden' (31 49 24 S, 56 10 38 O); the claimed birth site is the nearby estancia Santa Blanca. This stop records the claim, not a fact.

stops.stop: Buenos Aires, the first legitimate identity card
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by Wikipedia (Spanish), 'Carlos Gardel', which dates 4 October 1920 to his first legitimate identity document, an Argentine cedula obtained on the strength of the Uruguayan certification. The research pool conflated the two documents by describing this one as listing him as Uruguayan; they are separate papers issued by separate states and are separated here. Pin is the canonical Buenos Aires coordinate, no office address being attested.

stops.stop: Buenos Aires, the oath of Argentine citizenship
stops.date_confidence: Both dates are attested by Wikipedia (English), 'Carlos Gardel': the application on 7 March 1923 and the oath on 1 May 1923. That article also carries the historians' reading that the timing was driven partly by a wish to avoid French conscription obligations ahead of a planned tour of France; the motive is an interpretation, not a documented statement of Gardel's. Pin is the canonical Buenos Aires coordinate.
